sentences.text: The petitioner is the 1st accused in C.C.No.244/2006 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Alappuzha (for short, the trial court).

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Alappuzha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 2(ix)(k), 7(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, the PFA Act) and Rules 32 and 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short, the PFA Rules) and Rule 10 of the KPFA Rules punishable under Section 16(1)(a) of the PFA Act.
2. The prosecution case in short is that on 8.12.2004 at about 10.30 am, the accused sold three packets of wheat powder each weighing 500 gms to the complainant.
After analysis by the Public Analyst, he opined that the sample is mis- branded.
3. PW1 to PW5 were examined and Exts.
P1 to P20 were marked on the side of the prosecution.
No defence evidence was adduced.

After trial, the trial court found the petitioner/1 st accused guilty for the offences under Sections 2(ix)(k), 7(ii) of the PFA Act, and Rules 32 and 50 of the PFA Rules and Rule 10 of the KPFA Rules punishable under Section 16(1)(a) of the PFA Act and 2025:KER:43468 he was convicted for the said offences.
The 2 nd accused was found not guilty and she was acquitted of the charges.
The petitioner challenged the conviction and sentence of the trial court before the Additional Sessions Court, Alappuzha (for short, the appellate court) in Crl.A.No.508 of 2009.
The appellate court dismissed the appeal.
This revision petition has been filed challenging the concurrent finding of the conviction and sentence of both the trial court as well as the appellate court.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that admittedly, the petitioner is not the proprietor or licensee and that as per the prosecution case, he is only a sales man and hence he could not have been convicted.

The learned counsel relying on few documents produced before this Court in Crl.M.A No.6937/2016 submitted that those documents would show that the 2nd accused is the licensee and hence the conviction of the petitioner is bad.

On the other hand, the learned Prosecutor supported the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence and argued that the necessary ingredients of the offences charged have been established by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
The learned Prosecutor further submitted that the documents produced by the petitioner at this stage cannot be entertained.

The prosecution case is that on 8.12.2004 at about 10.30 am, the Food Inspector visited the shop namely Koya's Industries running in Building No.VIII/3 of Aryad Grama Panchayat and purchased Seythu Muhammed vs State Of Kerala on 18 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81999244/
2 three packets of wheat powder from the petitioner who was present there.

sentences.text: The prosecution case in the complaint is that, the 2nd accused is the licensee of Koya's Industries.

The 1st accused had taken up a specific contention that he has no connection at all with the Koya's Industries and the business therein, apart from the fact that the building where the said business was running belongs to him.
It is true that Ext.P4 cash bill was issued by the 1 st accused.

For the simple reason that the petitioner was present in the shop room when the food inspector visited the shop and he issued Ext.P4 cash bill when the food inspector purchased the wheat powder, it cannot be presumed that he is the licensee or proprietor of the Koya's Industries.
At this juncture, it is pertinent to note Ext.P13 letter issued by the Aryad Grama Panchayat and the evidence of PW3, the Secretary of Aryad Grama Panchayat.
In Ext.P13, it is stated that the 2nd accused is the licensee of Koya's Industries.
It is also stated that she has applied for PFA license on 16.12.2004.
Ext .P13 has been proved through PW3.

The trial court as well as the appellate court took the view that though in Ext.P13 the 2 nd 2025:KER:43468 accused is shown as the licensee of Koya's Industries, she had applied for it only on 16.12.2004.

What is stated in Ext.P13 is that she had applied for PFA license on 16.12.2004.
6.
The petitioner produced some documents along with Crl.M.A.No. 6937/2016 before this Court as Annexures A1 to A4.
Normally, those documents cannot be entertained at this stage.
The petitioner could have produced the same during defence evidence at the time of trial.

But, considering the fact that the prosecution case itself is that the 2nd accused was the licensee and the letter of the Panchayat discloses that the license is in the name of the 2nd accused, I am of the view that Annexures A1 to A4 documents produced by the petitioner can be taken note of at this stage.

Annexure A1 is the provisional registration certificate issued by the District Industries Office,
Ambalapuzha in respect of Koya's Industries.
It would show that the 2 nd accused had obtained SSI registration in respect of Koya's Industries as early as in the year 2003.
The number shown in the document is the number of the building from where the sample was taken.
Annexure A2 license was obtained on 26.7.2006 by the 2 nd accused in respect of Koya's Industries in respect of said building to run the flour mill.

Annexure A3 is the certificate of registration under the Kerala Value Added Tax Rules, 2005 in respect of the 2025:KER:43468 very same building issued in the year 2007 and Annexure A4 is the license issued by the Aryad Grama Panchayat for the period 2007-2008.
Annexures A1 to A4 corroborate the evidence of PW3 that the 2nd accused is the licensee of the building in question at the relevant point of time.
In these circumstances, I am of the view that the conviction and sentence of the petitioner on the ground that he was the proprietor of the business namely Koya's Industries cannot be sustained.
Accordingly, the conviction and sentence of the petitioner as per the impugned judgments of the trial court as well as the appellate court are set aside.
He is acquitted of the charges levelled against him.
This Crl.R.P is allowed.
